market_holds: There is no option chain (sealed baseline), so the usual move is the only guide. The baseline puts the close-to-close median at 3.4%. Measured at the opening print, which is the scored window, the last three prints moved +5.3% (Q4'25: close 24.89, open 26.22), +1.0% (Q1'26: 36.38 to 36.74) and -9.3% (Q2'26: 50.00 to 45.37), from Yahoo daily bars. The stock is at 66.72, 1.1% below its 52-week high and +33% since the Q2 print. It is +13% over 20 sessions, mostly from 7 Oct to 4 Nov (55.34 to 67.46), while SPY was flat to down. On 5 Nov, when SPY fell 4.4%, ANDG fell only 1.8%, so the run-in is the stock's own and not the tape. The only company news in the run-in was the 15 Oct release on closed acquisitions (19 deals signed, about $190m annualised). The CBIZ/Grant Thornton deal dates from 29 Jul, so it is not this run-in. The stock trades above the sell-side average target: about $61.3 average and $58 median across 8 analysts per StockAnalysis (updated 9 Nov), with UBS at $78 on 9 Nov. Q3 revenue consensus is about $334-340m (Chartmill/FXEmpire $340.3m, revised down about 1.1% over 3 months; EarningsWhispers $334.4m). That is +18-20% on Q3'25's $284.3m. FY26 revenue consensus is $992.8m, inside the guide of $980m-$1.0bn, with EPS at $1.87. The guide was reaffirmed on 12 Aug, and adjusted EBITDA guidance is $225-250m. The class A float is small: 18.4m shares after the August secondary (424B4), against 112.9m fully exchanged. Short interest was 2.4m shares on 14 Aug, about 6.6 days to cover (FINRA via curvedtrading, snippet only); I could not get a later reading. The lock-up for the August sellers, directors and officers ends 90 days after the 19 Aug prospectus, so around 17 Nov.
view: This is a beat-and-raise setup that the price has largely run ahead of. The inputs favour a good print. Q2 revenue beat the company's own $190-205m range by $12.7m. Organic growth ran at 20.6% against an annual guide of about 18%. The CEO said July and August 'far exceeded my expectations'. He also said he held the EBITDA guide by choice ('I'm a conservative guy') when the CFO had argued for raising it. And the revenue guide was held even though the expected 2026 acquisition revenue was cut from about $55m to $25-30m, which means the organic plan was raised by roughly the same amount. My own arithmetic: about 20% organic growth on Q3'25's $284m plus a few million from acquisitions puts Q3 near $345m, a little above consensus. With H1 at $458.4m and a normal Q4 (Q4'25 was $170m, so +15% gives about $196m), the year lands at or above $1.0bn, the top of the guide. On EBITDA, H1 was $122.8m (26.8% margin). Q4 is seasonally tiny (Q4'25 adjusted EBITDA was $9.4m), so the full year depends on Q3. Since Q1'26 ran at about 32%, a Q3 near 30% would put the year near the top of the $225-250m range. That supports a modest raise, not a large one. Against this, the price already holds a lot. The stock is up a third since August, sits above the average target and near its high, and has rallied 16% in five weeks with no company news. The Q2 analogue is instructive: a big beat on its own guide, a held guide, a +3% run into the day, and then a -9.3% open. So a beat alone is not enough here; the line it trades on is the size of the FY26 raise and any early colour on 2027 (at least $100m of annualised revenue from signed deals falls outside 2026). There is also a near-term overhang. The lock-up ends around 17 Nov with about 94m exchangeable units behind an 18m-share float. In August the follow-on S-1 came five days after the print, so holders may sell into strength. Shorts of about 13% of the class A float (August data) could amplify a good print. My net view: a small lean up on the fundamentals, offset by a crowded run-in and a high bar. The probability is not far from a coin flip.

recommendation.reason: The fundamental inputs point to a Q3 beat and a probable modest FY raise. The evidence is the CEO's stated conservatism, the CFO arguing on the call for a higher EBITDA guide, organic growth running above the guide, and the acquisition shortfall already absorbed. But I cannot show the price lacks this: the stock is +33% since the last print, +16% in five weeks without news, and above the sell-side average target. The last print sold off 9% at the open on a beat with a held guide, and the lock-up ends days later. Nothing here gets past 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A FY26 revenue guide lifted clearly above $1.0bn, plus an EBITDA raise past $250m and early 2027 colour that includes the $100m+ of signed-deal revenue, would push this firmly up. A guide held again, as in August, would make a sharp down open likely.

questions_pursued.question: Did the company give a Q3 guide, and how conservative is the FY guide?
questions_pursued.how: Q2 8-K exhibit 99.1, TradingKey transcript, Quartr and Finsee summaries
questions_pursued.answer: There was no Q3 range. The FY guide was held, and the CEO said explicitly that he chose not to raise EBITDA guidance against the CFO's advice. The organic plan was effectively raised to offset the acquisition shortfall.

self_critique: The case for leaning harder up: the CEO all but said the EBITDA guide is sandbagged, and the organic run-rate supports a revenue raise. Expected acquisition revenue is now locked in, sell-side estimates sit at the guide midpoint and so look stale against the run-rate, and shorts make up a meaningful part of a small float. A clear raise would plausibly gap the stock up 5-10% despite the run. The case for leaning down: the identical August setup opened -9%; a five-week, 16% rally without news looks like a whisper above consensus; the stock is above targets; and holders will want to sell into strength days before the lock-up ends. Neither side gets past about 60%, so I stay at 55 without a call.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition and the reminder to read the last reactions at the scored horizon (open, not close) mattered most here: the open move of -9.3% is far from the baseline's -3.4% close. P7's 'estimate the line from its inputs' produced a lean but not a confident one, because the price had visibly already moved with those inputs.
